sections.title: The causal principle and an absolute beginning
sections.rationale: This opening section groups the initial exchange over whether ordinary caused beginnings support a causal principle for the universe and whether appeals to nothingness explain that principle.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the causal premise that initiates the Kalam route, making it the principal constructive anchor of the opening section.
This move introduces the section’s central distinction between rearrangements of existing matter and an absolute material beginning.
This move develops the substances-versus-events distinction and continues the causal-principle exchange at a major structural step.
This move challenges whether quantified language about nothingness supplies an explanation, completing the opening causal exchange.

sections.title: Finitude of the past and concrete actual infinities
sections.rationale: This section follows the transition to a beginningless material alternative, the two finitude constructions, and the sustained Hilbert’s Hotel exchange over concrete actual infinities.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move supplies the principal beginningless-material alternative that frames the ensuing dispute about whether the past must be finite.
This move states the main actual-infinite construction from a beginningless temporal series to a finite past and cosmic beginning.
This move states the independent successive-addition construction and establishes the second principal route to temporal finitude.
This move introduces Hilbert’s Hotel as the concrete illustration used to develop the actual-infinite portion of the section.
This move introduces the critic’s governing distinction between unusual infinite behavior and metaphysical impossibility.
This move develops the competing roles of part-whole inequality and one-to-one correspondence within the infinite setting.
This move connects the dispute about metaphysical intuition to a proposed resolution of the inconsistent triad concerning infinity.
This move presents an alternative contextual treatment of infinite collections and continues the triad exchange without changing topics.
This move extends the hotel illustration to inverse operations and unequal remainders, adding a major step in the concrete-infinity dispute.
This move supplies the relative-complement formulation for the checkout cases and preserves the mathematical side of the exchange.
This move returns from formal relative complements to the claimed concrete subtraction problem and closes the hotel sequence.

sections.title: Beginningless countdowns and the scope of temporal finitude
sections.rationale: This section contains the later successive-addition exchange about a beginningless countdown, explanatory timing, descending-series paradoxes, and the qualification concerning metric and pre-metric time.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the principal asymmetry between an endless upward count and a beginningless countdown that has a terminal event.
This move introduces the earlier-completion problem for a beginningless countdown and begins the focused reply sequence.
This move identifies the disputed conditional direction and supplies the next major step in the countdown exchange.
This move shifts the exchange to a restricted explanatory demand concerning why the countdown terminates at a particular time.
This move offers preceding numbers and the counting rate as partial explanations, continuing the section’s explanatory-timing thread.
This move disputes whether the preceding number is the contextually relevant factor and completes the partial-explanation exchange.
This move broadens the successive-addition discussion with a descending Grim Reaper series as an additional structural illustration.
This move raises the section’s scope question by distinguishing the beginning of metric time from a possible pre-metric past.
This concession records the resulting metric-time qualification and the proposed relation between amorphous time and timelessness.

sections.title: Impersonal causation and timeless personal agency
sections.rationale: The final section groups the exchange over whether an impersonal indeterministic mechanism could initiate time and whether changeless or timeless consciousness is conceptually available.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the section’s principal impersonal indeterministic alternative to a personal explanation of temporal origination.
This move states the principal personal-agent inference from the timing of a universe arising from a nonphysical state.
This move introduces the conceptual challenge that consciousness requires change, extending the personhood exchange to timeless agency.
This move supplies the final interpretation of the freeze illustration and closes the exchange over timeless consciousness.

bridgeMappings.rationale: These retained moves distribute the defender’s complete motion route across the causal premise, both constructions for a finite past, and the concluding personal-agent inference.
Section 02 retains the central finite-past inference together with the Hilbert-style illustrations and replies used to connect concrete actual infinity to that inference.
These Section 02 moves preserve the hotel scenario, the intuition-based triad resolution, and the inverse-operation sequence concerning concrete infinite collections.
The initial successive-addition construction appears in Section 02, while Section 03 retains its countdown, explanatory-timing, and descending-series developments.
Section 04 retains both the inference from a finitely timed effect to personal agency and the later defense of timeless personal consciousness.
These retained moves carry the critic’s motion-wide route through challenges to the causal analogy, temporal finitude, concrete infinities, temporal scope, and personal agency.
The mapped moves retain the beginningless-material alternative and the challenges concerning actual infinity, countdown completion, pre-metric time, and impersonal origination.
Section 02 retains the critic’s full Hilbert’s Hotel line from the strangeness-versus-impossibility distinction through contextual language and relative complements.
Section 03 retains the countdown asymmetry, the conditional-direction diagnosis, and the proposed partial explanation for termination at the present.
Section 04 retains both the impersonal indeterministic alternative and the associated conceptual challenge to a changeless personal cause.
